title: Sovereignty and Pluralism: Who Rules Society?

scenes.text: Does your government truly hold all the supreme power over your life?
scenes.narration: Think about who really controls your world. Political thinkers call ultimate decision-making power sovereignty, and they fiercely debate whether it belongs to just one authority or to many.

scenes.text: A school principal manages rules, but sports captains and club heads run daily activities.
scenes.narration: As a helpful analogy, imagine your school. The principal has big rules, but sports captains and clubs guide your passions. Power is shared, not kept in one office.

scenes.heading: Monistic vs Pluralist Sovereignty
scenes.narration: Here is the big clash. Monistic theory says one state holds all undivided power, while pluralism insists that authority is divided among diverse groups because human life has many needs.

scenes.name: Harold Laski
scenes.idea: Authority must be federal because society itself is made of diverse associations.
scenes.narration: Thinker Harold Laski rejected absolute state power as an outdated legal fiction. He called the state a keystone of social architecture, meant to balance society rather than crush smaller groups.

scenes.quote: If society is federal authority should also be federal.
scenes.narration: Remember this key line for your exams! Laski believed that because you belong to families, unions, and clubs, no single government can demand your total, exclusive loyalty.

scenes.heading: Responsibility to Protect Framework
scenes.narration: Today, globalization redefines sovereignty from raw power to the responsibility to protect people. If a nation harms its citizens, the United Nations can step in as an accountable last resort.

items: Monism concentrates sovereign authority in the state
Pluralism distributes power among multiple social associations
Modern sovereignty means protecting citizens responsibly
scenes.narration: To wrap up, remember three big ideas: states share authority with associations, power is federal in practice, and modern sovereignty centers on protecting human lives.
